messages:
From: Anna Morrison <anna.morrison@vectorhealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@vectorhealth.com
Date: Tue, 3 Sep 2024 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API pricing — breakpoints vs blended approach

Karthik,

Thanks for the demo today — really helpful to see the latency and control you get with Redwood. Procurement forwarded me a template forecast (attached) so we can try to model cost for our two pilots (clinical summarization and triage routing).

Quick question on pricing architecture: our finance team is pushing for a single effective rate per token for budgeting (blended), while our engineering team prefers a marginal breakpoint ladder so higher-volume traffic benefits are explicit.

From VectorHealth's side, here are the rough numbers for the pilots: ~18M tokens/month initially, ramping to ~70M by month 6 (see attached forecast). We want to avoid surprises on month‑end true-ups and understand how a blended quote compares to a marginal ladder with breakpoints + true-up.

Can you send a short example that compares:
- a blended effective rate given a 12-month commit, and
- a marginal breakpoint ladder with monthly true-up and a clawback cap

Also, we have to include standard procurement constraints (POs, net30, and standard SLA language). Happy to loop legal after we land on economics.

Thanks,
Anna Morrison
Director, Digital Products
VectorHealth

Attachment: VectorHealth_Demand_Forecast_Q4-2024.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Anna Morrison <anna.morrison@vectorhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Sep 2024 09:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API pricing — breakpoints vs blended approach

Anna — great to meet you yesterday. Appreciate the forecast. I pulled a two-page proposal and a simple worked example (see attached Redwood-Proposal-v2.pdf) that shows both a blended effective rate and a marginal breakpoint ladder. High level:

- Blended: simpler for your finance team — a single $/token that already factors expected ramp. Easiest to budget but less upside if you materially outgrow the forecast.
- Marginal ladder: better if you expect non-linear growth; you see per-token discounts as volume passes breakpoints. We typically include a monthly true-up with a 90-day reconciliation window and an annual clawback cap to limit exposure.

My ask: can you confirm VectorHealth's appetite for a 12-month committed minimum vs a 6‑month pilot with option to convert? That will change the blended rate materially.

If ok, I also want to align internally on whether we can accept a capped clawback (we normally allow up to 15% annual clawback for forecast variance). Ben / Marissa — looping you for pricing guardrails and approval path.

Next steps: I can send a one-page comparison table that shows blended vs marginal across three ramp scenarios (flat / moderate / aggressive). Will also call to walk through the math if helpful.

Thanks,
Karthik
Account Exec — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood-Proposal-v2.pdf (proposal outline, includes worked examples)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Sep 2024 11:46:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API pricing — breakpoints vs blended approach

Ben / Marissa — forwarding VectorHealth thread and our proposal. Key asks from the customer: a clear blended effective rate for budgeting, and an alternative marginal ladder with monthly true-up + annual clawback cap. Forecast attached for reference.

Questions for pricing:
- Can we offer a 12-month committed blended effective rate at ~ $0.0009/token given the forecast (70M/mo by month 6)? If not, what floor do you want me to present?
- If we go marginal ladder, can we structure breakpoints at 0–25M, 25–50M, 50M+ with marginal discounts of 0%, 18%, 30% off list respectively and keep the annual clawback cap at 15%? Engineering wants clear per-token incentives (they'll route high-volume traffic); procurement wants a cap so finance is comfortable.
- Any redlines we should anticipate in legal around data retention or audit logs for a VPC/dedicated option? Customer asked only high level so far.

Ben — if you can greenlight the 18%/30% marginal discounts (and confirm effective blended math) I'll present both options in a short table and ask Anna which they prefer. If we need C-level approval for the marginal structure, let me know and I will escalate.

Thanks — Karthik

Karthik — thanks, and thanks to the pricing team for the quick turnaround. We reviewed Redwood-Proposal-v2.pdf with finance. A couple of clarifications before we route to legal:

1) VectorHealth preference: we prefer the marginal ladder for the pilot because it lets the product team clearly see per‑token economics as we scale. That said, finance requires a conservative blended-rate baseline in the contract for monthly reporting. Can you include both: the marginal ladder as primary billing + an appendix that shows the blended effective rate for forecasted usage?

2) Clawback: 15% annual cap seems reasonable. Please add an explicit 90-day reconciliation period for monthly true-ups (we prefer monthly usage statements and a single annual adjustment).

3) PO/terms: net30 is fine. For the pilot (6 months) we will include a renewal clause to convert to a 12-month committed term if performance goals are met.

If you can send an updated one‑page comparison and an outline of the contract appendix (blended calculation), we'll take that to legal and procurement. We attached the forecast again.

Best,
